outputs.L1: This disclosure relates to creating and configuring configurable forms, as well as creating and configuring configurable flow form process files. It further relates to automatically discovering some or all available actions that may be performed on a type of record from a set of form flow process files stored in a data store. Establishing a configurable form may include receiving a form file configured with an acceptability filter and at least one non-mandatory form item configured to be either on or off and included in the applicability filter; establishing at least one circumstance under which the non-mandatory form item is to be applied in the form file; and generating a configurable form file. On a graphical user interface, together with mandatory form items, non-mandatory form items may be displayed depending on the circumstances established by the applicability filter. A search list is also disclosed that can specify, without code, which data source should be used.
outputs.L2:
This disclosure concerns the generation and setup of configurable forms, the creation and configuration of configurable flow-form process files, and the automatic identification of some or all actions available for a particular record type based on a collection of form-flow process files stored in a data repository.  

Creating a configurable form may involve obtaining a form file that includes an applicability filter and at least one optional form element that can be set to an active or inactive state within that filter. It may further include defining one or more conditions under which the optional form element should be included in the form file, thereby producing a configurable form file.  

In a graphical user interface, required form elements may be displayed together with optional form elements, with the optional elements shown according to the conditions established by the applicability filter. The disclosure also describes a search list that can specify, without requiring code, which data source is to be used.
outputs.L3:
The disclosure relates to techniques for creating, configuring, and managing forms, as well as associated flow form process files. These techniques allow forms and form-driven processes to be defined in a configurable manner, reducing the need for custom programming when forms, actions, or data sources change.

In one aspect, the system is capable of automatically discovering available actions for a particular record type. The available actions may be identified from form flow process files that are stored in a data store. By examining these stored process files, the system can determine which actions are applicable to a given record type and make those actions available to a user or to another system component. This approach allows actions to be added, removed, or modified by updating the relevant process files, rather than by changing application code.

A configurable form may be generated from a form file. The form file can include an applicability filter and one or more form items. At least one of the form items may be non-mandatory, meaning that it is not always required to be displayed or completed in every situation. The applicability filter defines circumstances, conditions, or criteria under which particular form items, form sections, or form behaviors apply.

The non-mandatory form items can be selectively enabled or disabled based on the circumstances defined by the applicability filter. For example, a non-mandatory form item may be turned on and displayed in a graphical user interface when the filter conditions are satisfied, and turned off or hidden when the conditions are not satisfied. This allows the same configurable form to adapt dynamically to different users, record types, workflow stages, business rules, or data conditions.

In another aspect, a search list may be configured to specify which data source should be used for retrieving or displaying information. The data source selection can be defined through configuration rather than through hard-coded logic. As a result, administrators or other authorized users can modify the data source used by a search list without requiring software code changes, recompilation, or redeployment. This improves flexibility and maintainability while allowing the system to support different operational requirements or data environments.
outputs.L4:
The present disclosure relates to systems and methods for configuring, presenting, and controlling forms and form-driven processes in a graphical user interface. In particular, the disclosure addresses the use of configurable form files and flow form process files to determine which form elements and record actions should be made available to a user under particular circumstances.

In one implementation, a form may be defined by a form file that includes a plurality of form items. Each form item may correspond to a field, control, section, question, data entry element, display element, or other user interface component. The form file may include acceptability or applicability filters that specify when a particular form item is relevant, available, visible, editable, or otherwise applicable. These filters may be evaluated based on one or more conditions, such as the type of record being viewed, values already stored in the record, user role or permissions, workflow state, organizational context, selected options, or information obtained from an external or internal data source.

The disclosure further provides for optional or non-mandatory form items. Rather than requiring every potential item to be included in every instance of a form, the system may determine which optional items should be displayed or made available automatically. For example, a form item may be shown only when a selected category applies, when a related data value is present, when a particular process stage has been reached, or when a specified rule evaluates to true. This allows a single configurable form definition to support multiple use cases without requiring separate hard-coded forms for each variation.

The disclosed approach also includes flow form process files that may be used to define available actions for records. A process file may be associated with a data store and may specify actions that can be performed on a record, such as creating, viewing, editing, submitting, approving, rejecting, escalating, closing, reopening, assigning, or otherwise changing the status or content of the record. The available actions may be determined dynamically based on data-store values, record state, user identity, permissions, workflow conditions, or other defined criteria. As a result, the graphical interface can present only those actions that are relevant and permitted in the current context.

In some embodiments, the process files are data-store-based, meaning that the process definitions may refer to nominated data sources or data stores rather than requiring custom program code to retrieve or interpret the relevant information. A user, administrator, or configuration tool may nominate the data source from which form data, record data, action definitions, or filtering criteria are to be obtained. The system may then use the nominated source to evaluate form applicability, populate fields, determine available actions, and update records. This enables configuration of forms and processes without modifying underlying application code.

By combining form files having applicability filters with process files that define record actions, the system can automatically tailor both the displayed form content and the available workflow actions to the circumstances of a particular record or user session. Non-mandatory form items may be displayed when relevant and omitted when not relevant, reducing visual clutter and improving usability. Similarly, actions that are not applicable to the current record or user may be hidden or disabled, while relevant actions may be presented directly within the graphical interface.

This configuration-based approach allows form behavior, data relationships, and workflow actions to be changed by editing form files, filters, process files, or data-source nominations, rather than by rewriting software code. It therefore supports greater flexibility, easier maintenance, and faster adaptation to new business rules, record types, regulatory requirements, or organizational procedures. The disclosed system may be used in any environment in which records are created, reviewed, updated, or processed through configurable forms and workflows.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an invention about configurable forms, optional form fields controlled by applicability filters, configurable flow form process files, and automatic discovery of available record actions from stored process files.
counterfactuals.output: A system, method, and computer-readable medium are provided for generating and processing configurable electronic forms. A form definition includes a plurality of form fields and one or more applicability filters associated with optional fields, wherein the applicability filters determine whether corresponding fields are displayed, required, validated, or otherwise included based on contextual data, user input, record attributes, or process state. Configurable flow form process files define sequences of form states, transitions, validations, permissions, and record actions without requiring modification of application code. The system stores the process files in a repository and automatically discovers available record actions by analyzing the stored process files, including identifying actions applicable to a record based on record type, status, user role, and defined transition criteria. In response to a request for a record, the system dynamically presents applicable form fields and available actions, executes selected actions according to the corresponding process file, and updates the record and process state. The disclosed approach enables reusable, adaptable form workflows with runtime configuration of fields, flows, and actions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize a software disclosure involving GUI form configuration, mandatory and non-mandatory form items, acceptability/applicability filters, and no-code selection of search-list data sources.
counterfactuals.output:
The disclosure describes a no-code/low-code approach for configuring GUI forms and their search-list data sources.

A form is made up of multiple configurable items, such as fields, questions, or UI controls. Some items are mandatory, meaning they must be completed or satisfied before the form can be submitted or advanced, while others are non-mandatory and may be optional or conditionally shown.

The system uses filters to determine how form items are presented and used. These include:

- **Acceptability filters**, which define whether a given form item or value is acceptable in a particular context.
- **Applicability filters**, which determine whether a form item applies to the current user, record, workflow stage, object type, or other runtime condition.

The disclosure also covers configuring search-list or lookup fields without writing code. A user can select, through a GUI, the data source used to populate a search list, such as a table, dataset, object type, external source, or predefined query. The selected source may then determine what values appear in dropdowns, autocomplete fields, lookup dialogs, or other selection controls.

Overall, the invention enables administrators or non-programmers to define form behavior, required fields, conditional applicability, validation logic, and lookup data sources through configuration rather than custom software development. This allows forms to be adapted to different processes, users, or business rules while reducing the need for developer intervention.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a broad technical disclosure paragraph for a system that creates configurable forms and flow form processes, turns optional form items on or off based on circumstances, and auto-discovers actions for record types.
counterfactuals.output: A system is disclosed for dynamically generating and managing configurable electronic forms and multi-step form-driven workflows. The system may include a form definition engine configured to receive, store, and interpret metadata defining form sections, fields, validation rules, conditional logic, user roles, record types, workflow states, and process transitions. Based on such metadata and runtime context, the system may render one or more forms or flow-form interfaces, including single-page forms, wizard-style flows, approval flows, intake processes, update processes, and record-maintenance processes. The system may selectively enable, disable, show, hide, require, omit, or prepopulate optional form items based on circumstances including, without limitation, user identity, permissions, organizational role, record type, record status, prior user inputs, external system data, business rules, jurisdiction, date or time, device type, workflow stage, or detected events. The system may further include an action-discovery component configured to identify available actions associated with a given record type by inspecting metadata, schemas, configuration files, annotations, application programming interfaces, workflow definitions, permission models, plug-ins, service registries, or historical usage patterns. The discovered actions may include, for example, create, edit, submit, approve, reject, assign, escalate, archive, duplicate, request information, generate document, invoke external service, or initiate a related workflow. The system may automatically associate such actions with appropriate forms, buttons, menus, workflow steps, or process nodes, and may update the available actions dynamically as the record type, user context, system configuration, or workflow state changes. In some embodiments, the system separates form presentation from form logic and data persistence, thereby permitting administrators or automated tools to modify forms, conditional optional items, workflow paths, and available record actions without changing underlying application code.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an abstract in patent language for configurable form files where optional items are applied depending on filter conditions, displayed on a graphical interface with mandatory items, and linked to data-source nomination without coding.
counterfactuals.output: A computer-implemented system and method are provided for generating and rendering configurable form files. A form definition includes mandatory items and one or more optional items associated with respective filter conditions. Upon evaluation of the filter conditions against user, transaction, context, or data-source parameters, selected optional items are automatically applied to the form definition and displayed together with the mandatory items on a graphical user interface. The graphical user interface permits configuration of form content, item visibility, and data-source nomination through selectable controls, metadata, or configuration records, without requiring program code modification. Each form item may be linked to a nominated data source for population, validation, storage, or submission of corresponding values. The system thereby enables dynamic form composition, condition-based presentation of optional items, and data-source binding in a no-code environment.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
